method: A second pass over catalog names and geographic anchors. Blank map space is a discovery cue, not evidence that a culture lacks music. Selected configurations are scoped to the cited evidence; numeric axes, recording chain and optional instrument controls are authored models. Approximate cultural/documentation anchors are not territorial boundaries or claims of unique origin.

entries.name: Famo (Basotho accordion song)
entries.configuration: Basotho famo; a selected voice, accordion and drum arrangement of Lesotho’s popular song tradition.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Mohobelo (Basotho men’s dance song)
entries.configuration: Basotho men’s mohobelo dance song; a selected communal singing and clapping arrangement, with movement-led rhythm.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Litolobonya (Basotho women’s song and dance)
entries.configuration: Basotho women’s and girls’ litolobonya; group singing with sekupu tin drum and whistle cues.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Intore (Rwandan musical performance)
entries.configuration: Rwandan Intore performance music; drums support sung praise and poetry with coordinated dance. Drum construction and ensemble count are unspecified.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Burundi royal drum ritual repertoire
entries.configuration: Burundian royal-drum ritual performance combines synchronized drum patterns, dance, heroic poetry and traditional songs.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Moutya (Seychelles)
entries.configuration: Seychellois Moutya; men introduce topical verses and women answer over three goat-hide drums in a communal dance setting.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Tchiloli (instrumental theatre repertoire)
entries.area: São Tomé, São Tomé and Príncipe
entries.configuration: São Tomé Tchiloli theatre music; selected instrumental scene accompaniment with bamboo flutes, drums and seed-basket sucalos. Spoken dramatic dialogue is outside this configuration.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Nenets syudbabc (heroic narrative song)
entries.configuration: Tundra Nenets syudbabc heroic narrative; selected sung narrator with a repeating or commenting assistant. Epic performance roles are distinct from personal song.
entries.notes: Lukin describes an ideal narrator-and-assistant performance and also solo self-repetition; this seed chooses the former, without instrumental accompaniment.

entries.name: Nenets yarabc (first-person narrative song)
entries.configuration: Tundra Nenets yarabc; first-person narrative song, modeled with sung narration and an answering assistant. Genre boundaries vary between performers and collectors.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Nenets personal song repertoire
entries.configuration: Nenets individual song; selected unaccompanied voice carrying a personal melody and text, distinct from the heroic narrative genres.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Nganasan personal songs (hankudya baly)
entries.configuration: Nganasan autobiographical hankudya baly; a selected solo personal song anchored to documented performance in Ust-Avam.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Nganasan keingeirsya (sung dialogue)
entries.configuration: Nganasan keingeirsya; selected two-person sung dialogue from the documented genre, which also includes monologue performances.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Palauan chesóls (solo chant)
entries.configuration: Palauan chesóls; a selected unaccompanied solo chant configuration documented in the study Music Worlding in Palau.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Palauan ruk performance repertoire
entries.configuration: Palauan ruk; selected group vocal calls and hand percussion illustrating the documented layered vocal and bodily rhythms. The clapping card is a limited selection from the wider body-percussion practice.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Music of Terchová (string ensemble)
entries.configuration: Terchová music; selected small bowed-string ensemble and group singing, retaining the distinctive small two-string bass. The fiddle card represents the upper-string section; the alternative accordion ensemble is not combined here.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Horehronie multipart singing
entries.configuration: Horehronie unaccompanied multipart singing; a leader introduces changing melodic material and a chorus answers with relatively stable parts.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Bigwala (Busoga trumpet music and dance)
entries.configuration: Busoga Bigwala; five or more single-tone gourd trumpets interlock into a melody with accompanying drums, singing and dance. The trumpet card represents the ensemble.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Ma’di bowl-lyre music and dance
entries.configuration: Ma’di O’di song and dance repertoire; selected voice with the five-string plucked bowl lyre, used across social and ceremonial occasions.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Chopi timbila orchestral music
entries.configuration: Chopi timbila orchestral repertoire; graduated-register wooden xylophones interlock over buzzing gourd resonators. This selected configuration includes the sung m’zeno section within the wider performance.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Gule Wamkulu (Chewa musical repertoire)
entries.configuration: Chewa Gule Wamkulu performance music; selected singing and drum accompaniment for masked dance. The practice extends across Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique; this anchor is not an exclusive origin claim.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Haida welcome-song repertoire (archive recital)
entries.configuration: Haida welcome-song repertoire; selected solo archive recital represented by the Folkways recording of a welcome dance for Edenshaw’s potlatch. This does not prescribe the full ceremonial ensemble.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Shuar anent
entries.configuration: Shuar anent; selected unaccompanied intimate ritual song, distinguished from the festive nampet repertoire. This models vocal delivery and does not reproduce restricted texts or claim ritual efficacy.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Shuar nampet
entries.configuration: Shuar nampet; selected vocal-only festive song recital. Instruments documented elsewhere in Shuar culture are not automatically assigned to this performance.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.

entries.name: Al-Ayyala (Oman and UAE)
entries.area: Al Buraimi–Al Ain cultural region, Oman / UAE
entries.configuration: Al-Ayyala of Oman and the UAE; facing rows chant poetry to large and small drums, tambourines and brass cymbals. The anchor represents a shared cross-border practice.
entries.notes: Selected arrangement; contemporary field-recording chain and numeric axes are authored modeling choices.
